notes: Searches used: 16. First-pass counts refer to the 69 draft sentences (c01-c69); replacement and added sentences are listed after c69 with ids ending r or n. Textbook (2): systolic and diastolic definitions, kept once in section 3; the duplicates in the FAQ and key facts were removed to stay under the cap. Not found in retrieved text and removed: BHF 'up to three types' of medicine; 'losing weight is all that is needed'; BHF fruit/veg/saturated fat advice; 'important not to stop without speaking to the GP' (reworded to NHS 'do not stop if side effects' plus Blood Pressure UK and CDC); sleepiness as a side effect; NHS Health Checks; thiazide diuretics and alpha-blockers named by the NHS; the NHS pregnancy-planning advice attributed to NHLBI. Search summaries disagreed once on whether NHS inform lists regular nosebleeds (one summary said no, two later queries said yes); the page keeps the claim, worth a human glance at the NHS inform page. NHLBI causes page returned only its opening line on medicines; the named medicine list comes from an NHLBI news item and is worded as 'linked to'. CONTRADICTIONS/UNSUPPORTED in the EXISTING entry (not edited): (1) definition/seekCare use thresholds (140/90, 135/85, 180/120): NHS gives 140/90 clinic and 135/85 home, consistent, but MedlinePlus (US) defines high BP as 130/80 or higher, so the page is NHS-specific; the 180/120 same-day route for readings alone was not retrieved from any UK source (NHLBI, US, says above 180/120 needs immediate attention). (2) overview: 'one adult in three', 'half do not know', 'single biggest contributor to stroke and heart disease worldwide', 'treatment is cheap and effective' not retrieved. (3) causes: 'over 90%' primary, adrenal tumours, narrowed renal arteries not retrieved; MedlinePlus lists kidney disease, adrenal disorders, pregnancy, medicines, sleep apnoea. (4) symptoms list includes dizziness: NHS lists headaches, blurred vision, chest pain (NHS inform adds double vision, nosebleeds, shortness of breath); dizziness not retrieved. (5) treatment: 'most people need two or more' - NHS only says more than one may be needed; 'thiazide-like diuretics' not retrieved from NHS text (NICE not returned in full). (6) riskFactors: 'Black African or Caribbean ancestry' not retrieved as a risk factor (NHS only says ethnicity affects which medicine is offered first). (7) signs: 'retinal changes, enlarged heart, kidney damage' only partly retrieved (MedlinePlus: thickened heart muscle). (8) complications: aortic dissection and retinopathy not retrieved by name (NHS inform: aortic aneurysm; MedlinePlus Genetics: eye problems). (9) prevention 'moderate alcohol' - NHS says cutting back on alcohol.
